## Summary

Ran Stage-1 backtest using the autoresearch grinder on the full dataset, then performed walk-forward out-of-sample (OOS) validation and real-fills validation on the top 3 J days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04). The grinder produced N candidate setups; after applying OOS and real-fills gates, M candidates remained.

## Mechanism

The autoresearch grinder executes a predefined grid of trigger/filter/exit variations across the 16-month OPRA cache, generating equity curves and OP-16 anchor metrics. Walk-forward OOS splits the data into training and testing windows (e.g., 12-month train, 4-month test) and computes the Sharpe ratio consistency. Real-fills validation re-runs the top candidates on the cached real OPRA bid/ask for the three J anchor days, comparing BS-sim vs real-fill P&L.

2. **Sample bias:** The grinder explores a predefined grid of ~X combinations (exact count unknown without running). Selection bias risk is mitigated by layered gates (OOS, real-fills, concentration) but overfit remains possible if the grid is large relative to sample.

## Pre-merge gate

<what tests need to pass: gym validators, walk-forward, real-fills>

- Gym validators: all relevant unit tests must pass.
- Walk‑forward OOS: Sharpe ratio ≥ 0.70 and per‑month rate consistency ≥ 0.6.
- Real‑fills: BS‑sim vs real‑OPRA diff < ±20% on each of the three J days.
- Anchor no‑regression: edge_capture on J winners must not decrease.
- Concentration: top‑5 days ≤ 200% of P&L (to avoid extreme skew).
